title: Ideological Bias in LLMs' Economic Causal Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2604.21334v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Do large language models (LLMs) exhibit systematic ideological bias when reasoning about economic causal effects? As LLMs are increasingly used in policy analysis and economic reporting, where directionally correct causal judgments are essential, this question has direct practical stakes. We present a systematic evaluation by extending the EconCausal benchmark with ideology-contested cases - instances where intervention-oriented (pro-government) and market-oriented (pro-market) perspectives predict divergent causal signs. From 10,490 causal triplets (treatment-outcome pairs with empirically verified effect directions) derived from top-tier economics and finance journals, we identify 1,056 ideology-contested instances and evaluate 20 state-of-the-art LLMs on their ability to predict empirically supported causal directions. translated_title: 大语言模型经济因果推理中的意识形态偏见
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在推理经济因果效应时是否会表现出系统性的意识形态偏见？随着大语言模型越来越多地被应用于政策分析和经济报道——在这些领域中，方向正确的因果判断至关重要——这一问题具有直接的现实意义。我们通过在EconCausal基准中扩展加入意识形态争议案例来开展系统性评估——即干预导向（亲政府）视角与市场导向（亲市场）视角会预测出相反因果符号的实例。我们从顶级经济学和金融学期刊中提取的10,490个因果三元组（具有经验验证效应方向的处理-结果对）中，识别出1,056个意识形态争议实例，并评估了20个最先进的大语言模型预测经验支持的因果方向的能力。我们发现，意识形态争议项目始终比非争议项目更难预测，并且在17个o……
tldr: 该研究在EconCausal基准中引入亲政府与亲市场观点存在分歧的意识形态争议案例，发现大语言模型在经济因果推理中表现出系统性意识形态偏见，且争议性案例的因果方向预测难度显著更高。
en_tdlr: By extending the EconCausal benchmark with 1,056 ideology-contested causal cases where pro-government and pro-market perspectives diverge, this study shows that LLMs exhibit systematic ideological bias in economic causal reasoning, with contested items being consistently harder to predict than non-contested ones.
